decision_reason: NASA's current Software Catalog identifies CPR* as the open-source LAR-19679-1 release and links this repository. The repo is a versioned 1.0.0 C implementation of the standard ADS-B/TIS-B Compact Position Reporting functions, includes fixed- and floating-point formal verification artifacts, and carries NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3. NASA technical records state its formally verified reference implementation was incorporated into the governing standard. The source is quiet since 2020, but NASA's current exact-product catalog page continues to distribute this same repository.

government_provenance.note: NASA's LAR-19679-1 Software Catalog page identifies CPR* and links Download Now directly to the assigned nasa/cpr repository. The repository README names NASA Langley Research Center as the contact/developer office.

public_source.note: The public repository provides fixed- and floating-point C implementations, formal specifications/proofs, verification artifacts, and README/version information without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The assigned product repository contains its exact NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 grant (NOSA-1.3); README expressly says CPR* is released under NASA's Open Source Agreement. The first public code-and-license release is https://github.com/nasa/cpr/commit/08bdb34d1e4228359248d6054307e97417c060f6 (2019-10-02).

primary_evidence.note: NASA's 2022 Langley presentation says the formal analysis produced a formally verified CPR reference implementation incorporated in the governing ADS-B standard. NASA's exact current LAR-19679-1 page offers the versioned v1.0.0 implementation; the README explains the standard functions and the fixed-/floating-point proof artifacts.

product_identity: CPR*: a formally verified C reference implementation of the Compact Position Reporting functions used by ADS-B/TIS-B; fixed-point and floating-point variants
agency: NASA Langley Research Center (LaRC), with National Institute of Aerospace research contributors
geography: United States federal aeronautics research; NASA Langley Research Center, Hampton, Virginia
license: NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 (NOSA-1.3) for the CPR* source and associated verification artifacts; Frama-C, PVS and Gappa tools are external dependencies
status_note: Maintained distribution exception: NASA's current LAR-19679-1 page still offers this exact source as open source. The repository's README states version 1.0.0; latest source changes date to 2020, but NASA's 2022 technical presentation says the formally verified reference implementation was incorporated into the governing standard. This is a standard implementation, not merely a mathematical predecessor or unrelated ADS-B tool.

decision_reason: NASA Ames identifies the Crisis Mapping Toolkit as its collection of geospatial crisis-response algorithms/utilities, and NASA's current ARC-17472-1 page offers the v1 release and links this exact source. The repository has Apache-2.0 source dating to 2014 and installation/how-to-use guidance for its Earth Engine map/UI and local processing tools. NASA currently distributes the exact toolkit as a reusable versioned product. External Google Earth Engine/PyQt dependencies are not part of the repository license.

government_provenance.note: The first-party README identifies the software as NASA Ames Crisis Mapping Toolkit and states it was developed by NASA Ames Intelligent Robotics Group with support from Google's crisis-response and Earth Engine teams. NASA's ARC-17472-1 catalog record directly links this repository.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes crisis-map processing algorithms, Python package/UI code, setup tooling and examples without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The root LICENSE and README state Apache License 2.0 for the toolkit source. The license was added in https://github.com/nasa/CrisisMappingToolkit/commit/a9535e47ddbf5839083cce32f51cfb17944751fb (2014-12-05); externally operated Google Earth Engine and PyQt dependencies remain under their own terms.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's current ARC-17472-1 page identifies Crisis Mapping Toolkit v1, describes its flood/damage/fire/population map products and Google Earth Engine role, labels it Open Source, and directly links the source. The README provides installation steps and examples for initializing Earth Engine, using the UI/map client, and local image processing.

product_identity: NASA Ames Crisis Mapping Toolkit (CMT) v1, a collection of geospatial image/satellite-data algorithms and utilities for generating crisis-response cartographic products
agency: NASA Ames Research Center, Intelligent Robotics Group; with Google Crisis Response and Google Earth Engine support
geography: United States federal Earth-science and disaster-response research; NASA Ames Research Center, California

status_note: Maintained distribution: NASA's current catalog lists CMT v1 and directly links the exact repository. README supplies install/use guidance; external Earth Engine access and PyQt dependencies are not bundled or covered by the root Apache grant. The newest repository maintenance is within the current NASA catalog distribution period; do not imply the toolkit licenses Google Earth Engine or its datasets.

decision_reason: NASA Goddard's current cFS catalog lists and directly links the Checksum App, explaining its onboard memory-integrity role. The exact repository has active source changes through September 2026, current Apache-2.0 coverage, versioned app release history, and a generated user guide. The first public licensed code release is CS 2.4.0 under the included NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 in 2017. This is the reusable cFS CS application, distinct from cFE and other apps.

government_provenance.note: NASA Goddard's current cFS catalog lists the Checksum App (CS), describes it as memory integrity management, and links directly to nasa/CS. The cFS team page identifies the framework/apps as developed by NASA Goddard.

public_source.note: The active public dev branch contains the flight-software application source, build/configuration files, tests and CS user-guide documentation; GitHub history shows substantive/app-support updates through 2026-09-24.

eligible_license.note: The current dev-branch root LICENSE is Apache-2.0. The earliest verified functional source release was CS 2.4.0 with the NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 PDF included in commit https://github.com/nasa/CS/commit/1381075e8d3c21dd9faade60514159d48d196662 (2017-07-01). NOSA-1.3 is OSI-approved; the present source is directly covered by Apache-2.0.

primary_evidence.note: The NASA catalog explains that CS checks critical flight-memory regions and reports unexpected changes to ground operators, and the repository README/user guide explain its configuration and use within a cFS deployment. The exact app is a reusable cFS flight-software function, not a sample/lab utility.

agency: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), Core Flight System team

decision_reason: The assigned repository is a public Salesforce package with no repository-wide source-code license. NASA's exact MSC-26882-1 Contact Tracing and Tracking page classifies the product as a U.S. Government Purpose Release and expressly limits use to federal employees and government contractors. This is not an eligible public OSS release; reject from the OSS catalog even though NASA documented historical internal use.

government_provenance.note: NASA's MSC-26882-1 page identifies the CTT application and states that NASA's Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer and Office of the Chief Information Officer developed it. The assigned nasa/CTT repository exposes a Salesforce package named CTT_Package, consistent with that product.

public_source.note: The public GitHub repository exposes Salesforce package metadata, Lightning components, Apex code and documentation without credentials. Public visibility does not itself grant rights to copy or reuse.

eligible_license.note: The NASA Software Catalog classifies MSC-26882-1 as a U.S. Government Purpose Release and says it is only available for federal employees/contractors; no OSS license or source-code grant is present in the repository root. This is not an OSI-approved public code grant.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's official 2021 OCIO annual report documents agency deployment of the CTT application for pandemic operations; the exact NASA catalog page describes the contact-tracing workflow at NASA installations. These establish historic product identity/use, but do not overcome the restricted release/license failure.

agency: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer and NASA Office of the Chief Information Officer

decision_reason: This is a distinct Python developer client for NASA's Cumulus Framework API, not the Cumulus service, API server or dashboard. The repository provides installation, authentication/configuration, examples and operations for calling the same API used by the dashboard; its current setup metadata versions the package as 3.2.2 and code was updated through April 2026. The root Apache-2.0 grant accompanied the initial functional 2020 source. NASA identifies Cumulus as an ESDIS-developed open-source framework and currently publishes versioned API docs and framework releases.

government_provenance.note: The exact client README links the NASA Cumulus Framework and API. NASA's first-party framework README says Cumulus is an open-source data-ingest/archive/distribution/management system developed for NASA Earth Science data streams; NASA Earthdata identifies it as an ESDIS project.

public_source.note: The public Python package source, examples, setup/config files and usage docs are available without credentials; the repository's latest package/version changes were made 2026-04-23.

eligible_license.note: The actual root LICENSE is Apache License 2.0 for this client source. The first public functional source snapshot already included LICENSE and package code at https://github.com/nasa/Cumulus-API-Python/commit/e614bf40e9a32b7df300e388b10edee21d7dfefb (2020-05-12).

primary_evidence.note: NASA's current API docs publish versioned Cumulus API references for client integrations; the client README gives installation, initialization/auth configuration and working examples for create/edit/delete/query tasks. NASA's Cumulus framework repo documents releases through v22.3.5 (2026-08-14), and the client repo itself updated package configuration in April 2026.

agency: NASA Earth Science Data and Information System (ESDIS) Project, Cumulus Core team
